To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the structure and function of Neurospora crassatyrinase is similar to that of the copper complex of hemocyanins and that the catalytic properties of the enzyme are consistent with the proposed mechanism of the copper complex.

(1) the active site copper complex of Neurospora crassatyrosinase is composed of two Cu atoms bridged by a hydroxyl group; (2) the copper atoms are coordinated by three histidine and one glutamate ligands; (3) the active site is located in an extended hydrophobic cleft; (4) the copper complex in Neurospora tyosinase is very similar to that in the oxygen binding protein hemocyanin;
the structure of the active site of tyrosinase is very similar to that of the hemocyanins and that the catalytic cycle is very different from that of the hemoproteins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of the catalytic mechanism of tyrosinase and its role in the formation of melanins and other polyphenols in biological systems.
the molecular mechanism of the enzymatic reaction catalyzed by tyrosinase and with the role of the copper complex of this enzyme in the catalysis.
the elucidation of the structural and catalytic properties of tyrosinase, which is a copper containing enzyme involved in melanin formation and the oxidation of various phenolic compounds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

Neurospora tyrsinase is a very promising model for the elucidation of the mechanism of action of tyrosinases and hemocyanins, and that the results obtained with this enzyme are of general interest for the field of copper proteins.

Neurospora tyosinase and hemocyanin are structurally and catalytically very similar, and the structural and catalytic differences between the two proteins are due to the differences in the amino acid sequence.

the binuclear active sites of Neurospora crassatyrinase and hemocyanin are similar, and that the copper complex in both proteins is capable of binding molecular oxygen and activating it for the oxidation of phenolic substrates.
